items.text:
आत्मापराधवृक्षस्य फलान्येतानि देहिनाम् ।
दारिद्र्य-रोग-दुःखानि बन्धनव्यसनानि च ॥१॥
items.tr:
ātmāparādhavṛkṣasya phalānyetāni dehinām |
dāridrya-roga-duḥkhāni bandhanavyasanāni ca ||1||
items.en: Poverty, disease, sorrow, captivity and misfortune are the fruits that grow on the tree of a person's own wrongdoing.

items.text:
पुनर्वित्तम्पुनर्मित्रं पुनर्भार्या पुनर्मही ।
एतत्सर्वं पुनर्लभ्यं न शरीरं पुनः पुनः ॥२॥
items.tr:
punarvittampunarmitraṃ punarbhāryā punarmahī |
etatsarvaṃ punarlabhyaṃ na śarīraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||2||
items.en: Wealth can be gained again, a friend again, a wife again, land again; all these can be had again, but not this human body.

items.text:
बहुनां चैव सत्त्वानां समवायो रिपुञ्जयः ।
वर्षन्धाराधरो मेघस्तृणैरपि निवार्यते ॥३॥
items.tr:
bahunāṃ caiva sattvānāṃ samavāyo ripuñjayaḥ |
varṣandhārādharo meghastṛṇairapi nivāryate ||3||
items.en: When many beings join together they defeat the enemy; even blades of grass, woven together, keep out the rain from a pouring cloud.

items.text:
जलै तैलं खले गुह्यं पात्रे दानं मनागपि ।
प्राज्ञे शास्त्रं स्वयं याति विस्तारे वस्तुशक्तितः ॥४॥
items.tr:
jalai tailaṃ khale guhyaṃ pātre dānaṃ manāgapi |
prājñe śāstraṃ svayaṃ yāti vistāre vastuśaktitaḥ ||4||
items.en: Oil on water, a secret told to a wicked person, a gift to a worthy person however small, and knowledge given to a wise person all spread out by their own nature.

items.text:
धर्माख्याने श्मशाने च रोगिणां या मतिर्भवेत् ।
सा सर्वदैव तिष्ठेच्चेत्को न मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥५॥
items.tr:
dharmākhyāne śmaśāne ca rogiṇāṃ yā matirbhavet |
sā sarvadaiva tiṣṭheccetko na mucyeta bandhanāt ||5||
items.en: If the mind we have while hearing a religious talk, at a cremation ground, or during sickness stayed with us always, who would not be set free?

items.text:
उत्पन्नपश्चात्तापस्य बुध्दिर्भवति यादृशी ।
तादृशी यदि पूर्वं स्यात्कस्य स्यान्न महोदयः ॥६॥
items.tr:
utpannapaścāttāpasya budhdirbhavati yādṛśī |
tādṛśī yadi pūrvaṃ syātkasya syānna mahodayaḥ ||6||
items.en: If the good sense that comes after regret came before the act, who would not do well in life?

items.text:
दाने तपसि शौर्यं वा विज्ञाने विनये नये ।
विस्मयो न हि कर्तव्यो बहुरत्ना वसुन्धरा ॥७॥
items.tr:
dāne tapasi śauryaṃ vā vijñāne vinaye naye |
vismayo na hi kartavyo bahuratnā vasundharā ||7||
items.en: Do not be proud of your giving, penance, courage, knowledge, modesty or good judgement; the earth holds many such jewels.

items.text:
दरस्थोऽपि न दूरशो यो यस्य मनसि स्थितः ।
यो यस्य हृदये नास्ति समीपस्थोऽपि दूरतः ॥८॥
items.tr:
darastho'pi na dūraśo yo yasya manasi sthitaḥ |
yo yasya hṛdaye nāsti samīpastho'pi dūrataḥ ||8||
items.en: One who lives in someone's mind is not far away even when far; one who is not in someone's heart is far away even when near.

items.text:
यस्माच्च प्रियमिच्छेतु तस्य ब्रूयात्सदा प्रियम् ।
व्याधो मृगवधं गन्तुं गीतं गायति सुस्वरम् ॥९॥
items.tr:
yasmācca priyamicchetu tasya brūyātsadā priyam |
vyādho mṛgavadhaṃ gantuṃ gītaṃ gāyati susvaram ||9||
items.en: Always speak pleasantly to the one you want something from; the hunter sings sweetly when he goes to kill the deer.

items.text:
अत्यासन्ना विनाशाय दूरस्था न फलप्रदाः ।
सेव्यतां मध्यभागेन राजविह्निगुरुस्त्रियः ॥१०॥
items.tr:
atyāsannā vināśāya dūrasthā na phalapradāḥ |
sevyatāṃ madhyabhāgena rājavihnigurustriyaḥ ||10||
items.en: Being too close to a king, fire, a teacher or women leads to ruin, and staying too far brings no benefit; deal with them from a middle distance.

items.text:
अग्निरापः स्त्रियो मूर्खाः सर्पो राजकुलानि च ।
नित्यं यत्नेन सेव्यानि सद्यः प्राणहराणि षट् ॥११॥
items.tr:
agnirāpaḥ striyo mūrkhāḥ sarpo rājakulāni ca |
nityaṃ yatnena sevyāni sadyaḥ prāṇaharāṇi ṣaṭ ||11||
items.en: Fire, water, women, fools, snakes and royal families must always be handled with care, for these six can take life in an instant.

items.text:
स जीवति गुणा यस्य यस्य धर्मः स जीवति ।
गुणधर्मविहीनस्य जीवितं निष्प्रयोजनम् ॥१२॥
items.tr:
sa jīvati guṇā yasya yasya dharmaḥ sa jīvati |
guṇadharmavihīnasya jīvitaṃ niṣprayojanam ||12||
items.en: He truly lives who has good qualities and righteousness; the life of one without good qualities and righteousness is useless.

items.text:
यदिच्छसि वशीकर्तुं जगदेकेन कर्मणा ।
पुरः पञ्चदशास्येभ्यो गां चरन्तीं निवारय ॥१३॥
items.tr:
yadicchasi vaśīkartuṃ jagadekena karmaṇā |
puraḥ pañcadaśāsyebhyo gāṃ carantīṃ nivāraya ||13||
items.en: If you wish to win over the world by one single act, keep your tongue, like a wandering cow, from grazing in front of the fifteen mouths of the senses.

items.text:
प्रस्तवासदृशं वाक्यं प्रभावसदृशं प्रियम् ।
आत्मशक्तिसमं कोपं यो जानाति स पण्डितः ॥१४॥
items.tr:
prastavāsadṛśaṃ vākyaṃ prabhāvasadṛśaṃ priyam |
ātmaśaktisamaṃ kopaṃ yo jānāti sa paṇḍitaḥ ||14||
items.en: One who knows how to speak words that suit the occasion, show kindness that suits his position, and show anger that matches his strength is wise.

items.text:
एक एव पदार्थस्तु त्रिधा भवति वीक्षितः ।
कुणपंकामिनी मांसं योगिभिः कामिभिः श्वभिः ॥१५॥
items.tr:
eka eva padārthastu tridhā bhavati vīkṣitaḥ |
kuṇapaṃkāminī māṃsaṃ yogibhiḥ kāmibhiḥ śvabhiḥ ||15||
items.en: One and the same thing is seen in three ways: a woman's body is a corpse to a yogi, a lovely woman to a lustful man, and a piece of meat to dogs.

items.text:
सुसिध्दमौषधं धर्मं गृहच्छिद्रं च मैथुनम् ।
कुभुक्तं कुश्रुतं चैव मतिमान्न प्रकाशयेत् ॥१६॥
items.tr:
susidhdamauṣadhaṃ dharmaṃ gṛhacchidraṃ ca maithunam |
kubhuktaṃ kuśrutaṃ caiva matimānna prakāśayet ||16||
items.en: A wise person does not reveal a well-made medicine, his own good deeds, the faults of his home, his love-making, bad food he has eaten, or bad things he has heard.

items.text:
तावन्मौनेन नीयन्ते कोकिलैश्चैव वासराः ।
यावत्सर्वजनानन्ददायिनी वाक् प्रवर्तते ॥१७॥
items.tr:
tāvanmaunena nīyante kokilaiścaiva vāsarāḥ |
yāvatsarvajanānandadāyinī vāk pravartate ||17||
items.en: Cuckoos pass their days in silence until the time comes for their song, which brings joy to everyone.

items.text:
धर्मं धनं च धान्यं च गुरोर्वचनमौषधम् ।
सुगृहीतं च कर्त्तव्यमन्यथा तु न जीवति ॥१८॥
items.tr:
dharmaṃ dhanaṃ ca dhānyaṃ ca gurorvacanamauṣadham |
sugṛhītaṃ ca karttavyamanyathā tu na jīvati ||18||
items.en: Righteousness, wealth, grain, the teacher's words and medicine should be received well and used properly; otherwise one does not live well.

items.text:
त्यज दुर्जनसंसर्ग भज साधुसमागमम् ।
कुरु पुण्यमहोरात्रं स्मर नित्यमनित्यतः ॥१९॥
items.tr:
tyaja durjanasaṃsarga bhaja sādhusamāgamam |
kuru puṇyamahorātraṃ smara nityamanityataḥ ||19||
items.en: Leave the company of the wicked, seek the company of the good, do good deeds day and night, and always keep in mind what lasts and what passes away.
